prompt: A job is 90% parallelizable and 10% strictly sequential. How much faster can it get with unlimited cores?
why: Speedup ≤ 1 / 0.1 = 10×, no matter how many cores.
trap: Adding cores feels linear until the serial part dominates.

prompt: Doubling the CI build machines from 16 to 32 cut the build only from 12 to 11 minutes, because linking runs on one machine and takes 10.
tells: linking runs on one machine and takes 10
why: The serial 10-minute link caps the gains; speed that up instead.
trap: It's not queueing; the parallel part already got faster.

prompt: A request spends 5 ms in parsing and 95 ms waiting on a database. Your teammate wants to make parsing 10× faster.
why: Speeding up 5% of the time by 10× saves 4.5 ms of 100. Optimize the 95 ms part.
trap: Amdahl's law applies to any speedup, not only parallel ones.

prompt: Moving model inference to 8 GPUs barely helped, because a single-threaded preprocessing step feeds them all.
tells: single-threaded preprocessing step feeds them all
why: The unparallelized step bounds total throughput; parallelize preprocessing.
trap: The GPUs are underused, not overloaded.

prompt: A test suite spends 2 minutes starting a database and 8 minutes running tests in parallel. Doubling the test runners won't get it under 6 minutes.
why: Doubling parallel work takes 8 min to 4, but the 2-minute serial setup stays, so 6 minutes is the floor at 2×.
trap: Adding runners can never beat the serial setup; shrink that first.

prompt: A service scales well to 8 cores, but past that throughput flattens because every request takes the same global lock for a short update.
why: The locked section is serial; as cores grow, it dominates and caps speedup.
trap: The lock is near saturation too, but the core insight is the serial fraction limiting parallel gains.

prompt: A MapReduce job uses 1,000 mappers that finish in 2 minutes, then a single reducer that takes 30 minutes. Adding mappers is proposed to speed it up.
tells: a single reducer that takes 30 minutes
why: The single reducer is the serial fraction: even infinite mappers save at most 2 of 32 minutes.
trap: It's not a straggler problem; the reducer is serial by design.

prompt: Parallelizing image downloads made a page load barely faster, because one 3-second JavaScript bundle must finish before anything renders.
why: The blocking bundle is the serial part; parallel downloads only shrink the rest.
trap: Network speed matters, but the structure (serial gate) caps any parallel gain.
